source.title: Zero-shot self-supervised learning of single breath-hold magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) reconstruction
source.authors: Jinho Kim; Marcel Dominik Nickel; Florian Knoll

record.tranche_reason: Applies scan-specific self-supervised training and initialization comparisons to MRCP reconstruction and reports reconstruction quality and runtime; it does not test classification error.
record.gate_note: The study reports training and initialization outcomes for an MRI reconstruction task. Those results do not measure classification error or the specific initialization and shortcut conditions in the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study uses a ResNet regularizer and reports its MRCP reconstruction method's quality and runtime. It does not compare plain and residual networks, activation-matched initializations, normalization, or learning rates relative to a measured stability threshold. Pretrained versus random weights and frozen versus trainable stages do not test any listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that zero-shot reconstruction outperformed compressed sensing and the pretrained model for highly accelerated breath-hold MRCP, and that freezing early stages substantially reduced reconstruction time with a minor quality trade-off. These conclusions concern healthy volunteers and author-assessed image quality.
record.recipe_differences: Scan-specific self-supervised MRI reconstruction, not gradient training for image classification; uses an unrolled network with a k-space self-supervised loss and compares random with pretrained initialization.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization, frozen/trainable stage configuration, and learning rate; volunteer #11 required a reduction from 0.0003 to 0.0001 after instability prevented convergence at the initial rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Freezing 12 pretrained stages and training one stage reduced mean total reconstruction time from 136m16s to 20m25s with randomly initialized trainable weights, and from 78m46s to 18m19s with pretrained trainable weights. Some fine details and aliasing suppression deteriorated.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Freezing and caching pretrained stages can reduce scan-specific MRCP reconstruction runtime with a reconstruction-quality trade-off.

fits_no_version.finding: Pretrained trainable weights reduced mean total reconstruction time, especially with all 13 stages trainable; the authors also explicitly report faster convergence than with random weights.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretraining can accelerate scan-specific adaptation in this MRCP reconstruction architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: For volunteer #11, a learning rate of 0.0003 prevented convergence; reducing it to 0.0001 enabled satisfactory reconstruction. No stability threshold or curvature was measured.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning-rate tuning can be necessary for convergence in individual scan-specific MRCP reconstructions.

record.problems: Only 11 healthy volunteers; quantitative PSNR analysis used retrospectively undersampled data from two volunteers and an R=6 compressed-sensing reconstruction as reference. Image quality comparisons were visual assessments by the authors without radiologists or a reader study. A subject-specific learning rate was needed for volunteer #11.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and model-size or training-recipe qualifications.
Spurious local minima and extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training-error degradation with depth, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the special-initialization exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to the initial stability threshold, loss and curvature dynamics, edge-of-stability behavior, and divergence below the threshold.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: None of the rows warrants a verdict on V1–V6. Keeping total unrolled depth at 13 while changing backpropagation depth does not test V3. The constant trainable-parameter count across configurations also prevents interpreting these comparisons as width or capacity tests.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR training classification error; corrupted or random labels; model size, optimizer, and early stopping effects.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth comparisons for plain versus residual classification networks; special initialization for plain tanh networks; residual networks without normalization.
Activation-matched or orthogonal initialization, signal and gradient propagation, trainable depth in plain networks, and 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
Learning rates above a stability limit, curvature or sharpness dynamics, and divergence.
Batch normalization comparisons for training speed or learning-rate tolerance; Fixup comparisons.

rows.subject: zero-shot learning with random initialization across both datasets, 0/13 configuration
rows.operation_detail: Trained zero-shot reconstruction with no frozen stages and random initialization; measured PSNR and reconstruction time on two retrospectively undersampled acquisitions.
rows.value: PSNRs of 39.69 dB / 39.19 dB; reconstruction times of 102′12″ / 223′21″
rows.check: Numbers match the text, but these are reconstruction-method performance results and cannot establish any listed effect.

rows.subject: zero-shot learning with random initialization across both datasets, 12/1 configuration
rows.operation_detail: Trained with 12 frozen and one trainable stage; measured PSNR and reconstruction time on two retrospectively undersampled acquisitions.
rows.baseline: 0/13 random initialization: PSNRs 39.69 dB / 39.19 dB; times 102′12″ / 223′21″
rows.note: The text describes PSNRs as comparable and times as reduced; neither measure is classification error.
rows.check: Numbers match. Random initialization applies only to the trainable stage; the 12 frozen stages are pretrained. Freezing and caching stages measures a computational trade-off, not depth-induced training degradation.

rows.subject: zero-shot learning with pretrained weight initialization, 0/13* configuration
rows.operation_detail: Trained zero-shot reconstruction with pretrained weights for trainable stages and no frozen stages; measured PSNR and reconstruction time on two retrospectively undersampled acquisitions.
rows.value: PSNRs of 38.53 dB / 38.65 dB; reconstruction times of 81′35″ / 121′23″
rows.check: Numbers match. Pretrained-weight initialization is not the activation-matched or orthogonal initialization named in V4.

rows.subject: zero-shot learning with pretrained weight initialization, 12/1* configuration

rows.value: PSNRs of 38.63 dB / 37.30 dB; reconstruction times 24′24″ / 24′21″
rows.check: Numbers match. This is a reconstruction-method comparison, not a test of the listed initialization or depth effects.

rows.subject: zero-shot models with varying frozen and trainable stage configurations
rows.operation_detail: Compared average PSNR and training time across configurations from 0/13* to 12/1* on two retrospectively undersampled datasets.

conditions.value: two retrospectively undersampled datasets at R=25

rows.value: PSNR 37.97 ± 0.54 dB, median: 38.25 dB; reconstruction times decreased approximately linearly
rows.note: The text does not give each configuration's separate PSNR or training time here.
rows.check: The reported PSNR summary matches. The methods define reconstruction time as preprocessing, training, and final reconstruction together; the figure's training-time wording does not establish a separate optimization-speed measure.
